done_when: A follow-up that names a period the app reads itself (anything the app's date reader parses, such as last 30 days, explicit dates and date ranges, plus a month with or without a year, a year, a quarter with or without a year, or last, previous or this month, quarter or year) answers for that period whatever window the model emits; fiscal and other wording (FY, YTD, next month, previous week) keeps the model's window and the period control; a question naming no period still inherits or aggregates as before, and an amount is never read as a year; changing an answer's period still re-runs on the chosen period

findings.body: A thousands-formatted amount such as `Show actual amount 2,025` is still classified as calendar year 2025. `CALENDAR_YEAR_PATTERN` matches the digits after the comma, while the amount-context checks receive `Show actual amount 2,` and therefore match neither the direct-quantity nor linked-amount patterns. On a follow-up this overrides the inherited window with all of 2025. This is new evidence not covered by the ruling preserving `Actual to/of 2025`, and is distinct from the newly covered unformatted `actual amount 2025` case.
findings.title: Not done: an amount is never read as a year

findings.body: The new matrix and rerun checks still call `ChatService.ask` through `makeFixture`, where the model, executor/warehouse, audit, dimensions, reports, and resolver are fakes. Frontend period-control tests likewise mock the API, and the registered package test commands contain no Playwright/browser flow through a running API and real database. Thus named-period precedence, inheritance/aggregation, amount protection, and edited-period reruns remain proven only at mocked service/jsdom boundaries, contrary to the required end-to-end user-flow test. The successful close run does not close this prior test-audit blocker.
findings.title: Not done: end-to-end Ask coverage for period selection and reruns

why: An Ask question that names a period, such as July 2026, answers for that period even as a follow-up in the same thread; the model's own window and the previous answer's window used to win
